english: The fifteen observations $1^2,2^2,3^2,\ldots,15^2$ are grouped into the ten classes $[0,25),[25,50),[50,75),\ldots,[225,250)$, each class containing its left end point but not its right end point. Let $\bar{x}$ be the arithmetic mean of the fifteen observations, and let $\bar{x}_g$ be the arithmetic mean of the resulting continuous frequency distribution, computed with the class marks. Then $\bar{x}_g-\bar{x}$ is equal to
hindi: पंद्रह प्रेक्षणों $1^2,2^2,3^2,\ldots,15^2$ को दस वर्गों $[0,25),[25,50),[50,75),\ldots,[225,250)$ में समूहित किया जाता है, जहाँ प्रत्येक वर्ग में उसका बायाँ अन्त्य बिन्दु सम्मिलित है परन्तु दायाँ अन्त्य बिन्दु नहीं। माना $\bar{x}$ इन पंद्रह प्रेक्षणों का समान्तर माध्य है तथा $\bar{x}_g$ प्राप्त सतत बारंबारता बंटन का वर्ग चिह्नों द्वारा परिकलित समान्तर माध्य है। तब $\bar{x}_g-\bar{x}$ बराबर है
solution: Each observation is replaced by its class mark, so $\bar{x}_g-\bar{x}=\dfrac{1}{15}\sum(m_i-x_i)$, where $m_i$ is the class mark of $x_i$
solution_full: Check by errors: $\sum(m_i-x_i)=1262.5-1240=22.5$, and $\dfrac{22.5}{15}=\dfrac32$. Placing $225$ in $[200,225)$ instead would give $-\dfrac16$, which is option (B); the stated convention excludes it.
originality_note: New: the grouping error of the mean, i.e. the class-mark mean of grouped data minus the true mean of the same raw data (the squares 1..225), with an observation on a class boundary (way 5: ungrouped mean and grouped mean of one data set). Closest known: 'the mean of grouped data is only an estimate'. Different because: the question asks for the exact error, so the student must build the frequency table from the raw data, respect the boundary convention and compare the two means.
stem_review: Read as a student: every observation, class, symbol and condition is introduced before use, the class-boundary convention is explicit where it matters, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (exact fractions / sympy), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Stated the half-open classes so that 225 has one class. Changed: added the end-point convention.
key_step: Building the grouped table from the squares (225 goes to the last class) and comparing the class-mark mean with the true mean, or summing the per-observation errors.
justification: Two separate mean computations of the same data with a boundary trap that changes the answer; nothing is non-routine but precision matters. Above the direct table mean of 2023-P1-Q15 (L0) and the routine 2026-P2-Q12 (L2); comparable to the two-step checks of 2024-P1-Q3 (L3). Borderline 2/3.

concept_use.Arithmetic mean of ungrouped data: The true mean of the 15 squares, 1240/15, from the sum of squares formula.
concept_use.Arithmetic mean of a continuous frequenc: The class-mark mean of the grouped table, 1262.5/15.
